correctness.rationale: At per-transition quarter-turn rate γ=μ the diagonal telegraph signs are independent and the stationary beta exponent is zero; independent OU responses have variance h=D/μ. Here v₀ is the diagonal forcing amplitude specified by the SDE. Rotation preserves joint entropy and the marginal entropies agree. Integrating the trapezoid gives log(2a cos θ)+tan θ/2, yielding the stated information, derivative, and linear and cubic endpoints. At h>0 the second angular density derivative at zero is (xf)' + Var(U) f'', by differentiating smooth test-function expectations, and the first derivative vanishes. The densities and angular derivatives admit Gaussian envelopes after rotating the bounded uniforms and then adding the unchanged isotropic Gaussian. Entropy differentiation and integration by parts give the stated coefficient Var(U)J_h−1, strictly positive since the fourth cumulant excludes Gaussianity. The mixed fourth cumulant is −a⁴ sin²(2θ)/15 despite zero covariance, and strictness of Gaussian data processing follows from conditional Jensen on the likelihood ratio, since the positive kernel preserves access to every input set of positive product mass. For the entropy layer put L=A/√h and ρ(z)=G_b(z)−G_b(z+2L) on z≥−L. This is the normalized density on the right half; symmetry supplies the other half. For −L≤z≤0, −ρ log ρ≤1−ρ≤2G_b(−z); for z≥0, −ρ log ρ≤C√G_b(z). These envelopes are integrable uniformly for b in a bounded set. Thus the normalized entropy correction converges by dominated convergence and the cos θ prefactor contributes only O(ε²). Strict concavity gives positivity of the layer by averaging shifts. Differentiation at t=0 is dominated by shifted Gaussian bounds and Mills ratios; ∂²_tG_t at zero is G₀''/3 and integrating by parts gives K/3 for F(t)/t². Scaling z=tu gives the linear ramp, with Gaussian tail majorants outside |u|≤1 for t≥1, and hence F(t)/t→1. For the Fisher limit on the same half-axis at b=0, ρ≥cG₀(z) for L≥1 (separate z≤0 from z≥0 using the Gaussian tail ratio); |φ(z)−φ(z+2L)|≤φ(z). This gives the majorant φ²/G₀ and the two-edge coefficient K/a.
residual_risks: The limit is for fixed scaled angle t, not uniform over growing t. The numerical check of K is not an interval certificate. No finite-noise maximizer or trajectory statement was verified or claimed.

value.rationale: For a natural exactly solvable active-particle model the result quantifies dependence that covariance misses. The resolved angular layer gives both a sharp scale for the change from an athermal cusp to a quadratic response and a function describing intermediate noise-angle ratios, which neither endpoint expansion can supply. This is a useful benchmark for static position information, independent of possible uses in trajectory inference.
residual_risks: Restricted to the balanced rate, isotropic confinement and thermal noise model; no claim about signal inference, other turning dynamics or entropy production follows.
